sourceEvidence.label: ServerManager credential boundary, scoped access keys, machine authorization, audit, rate identity, and diagnostic data sources
sourceEvidence.sourceDrift: dirty: the uncommitted scoped access-key foundation on feature/secure-remote-mcp is part of the analysis target; the untracked deploy/ directory is user-owned and out of scope

assessment.summary: An embedded remote MCP server with OAuth browser consent lets an already-installed agent act with delegated, revocable, human-approved authority without a local connector or a pasted long-lived key.

nonNegotiables: No software may be installed on the operator's machine and no global agent configuration may be modified.
No reusable long-lived credential may pass through a chat window or a client configuration file.
Node bearer tokens, integration secrets, and raw agent URLs never reach a model-facing surface.
Grant revocation, owner demotion or deletion, membership change, and server-allowlist change take effect on the next tool call.
A machine principal never holds global administrative authority, whoever owns it.
Mutating actions require a live human approval on a ServerManager surface, not the MCP host's own prompt.
assumptions: Claude Code and Codex act as public OAuth clients on loopback redirects and cannot keep a client secret.
The MCP client may negotiate an older protocol version than the server's latest.
All Minecraft-authored text (log lines, mod names, MOTD, player names) is potentially adversarial.
No measured latency, session-count, or tool-call throughput target was supplied.
The deployment terminates TLS at a trusted reverse proxy which is already reflected in TRUSTED_PROXIES.

opportunities.title: Let an existing agent reach ServerManager with delegated, revocable, human-approved authority
opportunities.summary: Embed an OAuth 2.1-protected Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint in the existing API, exposing a narrow diagnostic tool facade plus a server-side action approval queue.
opportunities.diagnosis: The panel now has a machine principal but no interactive delegation flow, so the only way to point an agent at it is to paste a 90-day server-mutating bearer secret into agent configuration or a chat.

evidence.claim: Supported credentials are browser JWTs, single-use tickets, and scoped access keys; there is no interactive delegation flow.
Hash-only storage, mandatory bounded expiry, soft revocation, uniform invalid-credential errors, and throttled usage metadata are established patterns.
A reserved bearer prefix separates machine credentials from JWTs and machine credentials are header-only.
Machine bounds are evaluated before the global-admin bypass and machine principals are confined to the server route family.
Dangerous server operations already map to granular permissions usable as MCP scopes.
Password plus enabled-TOTP step-up with per-IP and per-account throttling and generic failures already exists.
The permission lattice defines group/leaf subsumption suitable for a scope vocabulary.
Audit rows can already name a human owner plus a machine credential.
The per-caller limiter is mounted inside the authenticated group, so unauthenticated OAuth endpoints would inherit no budget.
Indexed log events carry raw server-authored text, which is the primary prompt-injection carrier for any diagnosis tool.
Start/stop/restart persist intent, audit, and tolerate long agent calls; an approval queue must reuse those semantics.
Status, stats, and vitals are read with the decrypted node token, which must never reach a model-facing surface.
The control plane already owns identity, live RBAC, audit, and an authenticated browser session, making it the least-drifting host for both the authorization server and the tool facade.

desiredInvariants: effective authority = active OAuth grant ∩ unexpired/audience-bound token ∩ approved server allowlist ∩ approved MCP scopes ∩ the owner's live ServerManager RBAC
Consent requires a live human dashboard session and fails closed; machine credentials can never authorize other credentials.
Access and refresh tokens are high-entropy, stored only as hashes, never appear in URLs or logs, and are bound to the exact MCP resource.
An authorization code is single-use, short-lived, PKCE-bound, redirect-bound, and resource-bound.
Refresh rotation is replay-safe: reusing a rotated refresh token after a 30-second reuse grace revokes the grant; inside the grace it is a retry and gets a sibling pair.
The MCP endpoint exposes only named tools; no arbitrary URL, API path, shell, SQL, filesystem path, environment, node token, or console command is reachable.
No mutating action executes without a fresh human approval, a re-check of live authority, and an at-most-once atomic state transition.
MCP server instructions are static versioned application text; all returned server content is labelled untrusted evidence and is size-bounded and secret-redacted.

options.title: Remote MCP authenticated by a copied access key
options.summary: Serve the same MCP endpoint but authenticate it with the existing mcsm_pat_ bearer, configured by hand in the client.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Reuses the scoped-key authentication and intersection unchanged.
The interactive delegation gap remains; the human still handles a long-lived secret.
Tool-output bounding, redaction, and untrusted-evidence framing are still required.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authority is already bounded, but a reusable 90-day secret must be transported by hand and typically lands in a config file or a chat transcript.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Walk the real setup path for Claude Code and Codex and record every place the raw token comes to rest.

tradeoffs.assessment: One indexed hash lookup per call, identical to the existing key path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare tool-call latency against a JWT-authenticated equivalent request.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stateless request handling adds no retained per-client state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no session map grows under repeated stateless calls.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new failure domain; revocation is the existing soft-revoke.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Revoke mid-session and confirm the next tool call fails.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-client identity is only a key name, and rotation means editing client configuration by hand on every machine.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse rotating a key used by two clients and count the manual steps.

tradeoffs.assessment: Nothing new to store; ships as soon as the tool facade exists.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing access-key test suite unchanged.

residualRisks: A long-lived bearer secret is handled by a human and stored in client configuration.
No consent record identifying which client was authorized, when, or for how long.
Revocation granularity is per key, not per client session.

workPackages: Tool facade only; reuse existing bearer authentication.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP calls succeed with a scoped key and are bounded by the same intersection.
migrationNotes: Keep disabled by default so it cannot silently become the supported path.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the MCP endpoint; keys keep working on the REST API.

options.title: Embedded remote Streamable HTTP MCP with OAuth browser consent
options.summary: Add an OAuth 2.1 authorization server and a protected Streamable HTTP MCP resource to the existing API, with browser consent, durable grants, short-lived audience-bound tokens, and a server-side action approval queue.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adds the missing interactive delegation flow so no reusable secret is handled by a human.
Reuses hashing, expiry, revocation, intersection, step-up, and audit patterns for a second, separately stored credential family.
Requires new dedicated limits because OAuth endpoints sit outside the authenticated rate-limit group.
Bounded, redacted, explicitly-untrusted tool output reduces but cannot eliminate prompt-injection influence on the model.

tradeoffs.assessment: Delegation becomes an auditable, expiring, revocable grant made against a live MFA-capable session, and mutations require separate human approval; the cost is security-critical OAuth code inside the API process.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the protocol/authorization test matrix (PKCE, redirect, resource, code reuse, refresh replay, revocation, consent CSRF, intersection) and a real client smoke test.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each tool call adds a token-hash lookup, a grant reload, and a live RBAC check; diagnostics additionally fan out to the node worker.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure a diagnostics call end to end and confirm bounded fan-out and timeouts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Stateless Streamable HTTP keeps no per-client session; per-call allocations are bounded by explicit output caps.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no session growth under repeated calls and that output caps hold with adversarial log content.

tradeoffs.assessment: Grants expire and revoke independently and an interrupted action cannot double-execute; the API becomes responsible for one more protocol surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Race concurrent approvals and concurrent refreshes; assert exactly-once execution and family revocation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Owners see which client is connected, what it may reach, when it last acted, and can revoke in one click; every action carries owner plus client attribution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a full connect → diagnose → request → approve → execute → revoke drill and read the audit trail.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additive schema and additive routes; JWT, ticket, access-key, and worker protocols are untouched.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run fresh and upgrade migration tests plus the full existing API suite.

residualRisks: An OAuth authorization server is security-critical code in the API's trust boundary.
A hostile log line can still influence the model's narration even when it cannot widen authority.
An approved start/stop/restart is a real action on a real server; approval fatigue is a human risk the design can only bound, not remove.
Client-side token storage is outside ServerManager's control.

acceptanceCriteria: No token appears in a URL, a log, or a documented snippet.
Every tool call re-evaluates the full intersection.
An action executes at most once and only after human approval and a live re-check.
Tool output is bounded, redacted, and labelled untrusted.
migrationNotes: OAuth grants and tokens are stored separately from api_keys.
PAT authentication for MCP stays disabled by default.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Set the MCP feature flag off and revoke all grants; the additive tables stay until a maintenance window.

options.title: Local sidecar or device pairing
options.summary: Ship a small local MCP process that holds a device-bound key established through a one-time pairing code.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Removes the pasted secret, but only by installing software the request forbids.
Still needs a delegated control-plane credential and the same intersection and audit work.

tradeoffs.assessment: A device-bound key never traverses a browser redirect and can be hardware-protected, but the sidecar becomes a second place holding delegated authority.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model pairing-code interception, sidecar process isolation, and key storage on each supported OS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adds a local process hop for every tool call.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark stdio round trips against direct HTTP.

tradeoffs.assessment: A resident process per operator machine.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure idle RSS of the sidecar.

tradeoffs.assessment: Version skew between panel and sidecar becomes a supported failure mode.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define and test a compatibility window across sidecar versions.

tradeoffs.assessment: Install, update, and support burden on every operator machine, across three operating systems.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype packaging and auto-update for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

tradeoffs.assessment: Introduces a new distributable artifact and release channel alongside the panel.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define signing, distribution, and rollback for the new artifact.

residualRisks: A second delegated-authority holder on an endpoint the panel cannot attest.

workPackages: Defer unless remote OAuth proves uninteroperable with a required client.
acceptanceCriteria: A future phase records a verified client that cannot complete a remote authorization-code flow.
migrationNotes: The embedded OAuth resource remains the bootstrap and fallback path.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop distributing the sidecar; grants continue to work over remote OAuth.

opportunities.recommendation: Implement the embedded OAuth-protected MCP resource now; keep PAT authentication as a disabled-by-default fallback and revisit device pairing only if a required client cannot complete a remote authorization-code flow.

openQuestions: Whether the default MCP grant lifetime should be shorter than 30 days in production.
Whether dynamic client registration should be disabled once Claude Code and Codex both support client-id metadata documents.
Whether a future phase should let an owner pre-approve a narrow action (for example restart) within a short window instead of approving each request.
Whether action requests should be able to carry an agent-supplied diagnosis summary without that text becoming a phishing surface on the approval screen.
